emails.subject: Deadlines vs. schedules: which one is better for goal achievement?

paragraphs.en: Hey 張振輝,
paragraphs.zh: 嗨 張振輝,

paragraphs.en: I'm torn between the two.
paragraphs.zh: 我在這兩者之間猶豫不決。

paragraphs.en: On the one hand, I'm a big believer in setting deadlines when it comes to setting goals.
paragraphs.zh: 一方面,在設定目標時,我非常相信「設定截止日期」的重要性。

paragraphs.en: I think it's important to see our destination accompanied by a target date. It helps us to prioritize tasks. It also helps us to allocate our limited attentional resources (time, focus, etc.).
paragraphs.zh: 我認為,看見目的地並搭配一個目標日期是很重要的。這有助於我們排定任務的優先順序,也有助於我們分配有限的注意力資源(時間、專注力等)。

paragraphs.en: At the same time, I'm also a huge advocate of putting goal-oriented tasks on a schedule.
paragraphs.zh: 但與此同時,我也十分提倡把以目標為導向的任務排進「行事曆」中。

paragraphs.en: That way, we don't have to rely on willpower to do them. We simply note the time of day, check our schedule to see what we should be doing, and get to it.
paragraphs.zh: 這樣一來,我們就不必依賴意志力去完成它們。我們只需留意當下的時間,查看行事曆上該做什麼,然後去做就好。

paragraphs.en: Can these two tactics coexist?
paragraphs.zh: 這兩種做法能夠並存嗎?

paragraphs.en: There's a lot of talk about deadlines versus schedules, and which option leads to greater success.
paragraphs.zh: 關於截止日期與行事曆孰優孰劣,一直有很多討論。

paragraphs.en: Both tactics have their supporters and detractors. And some of these folks are pretty vehement about their opinions.
paragraphs.zh: 這兩種做法都各有支持者與反對者。有些人對自己的看法還相當堅持。

paragraphs.en: Here's the thing...
paragraphs.zh: 事情是這樣的……

paragraphs.en: You don't need to choose. In my opinion, you should set deadlines AND schedules whenever you set goals.
paragraphs.zh: 你不需要二選一。依我之見,設定目標時,你應該同時設定截止日期「與」行事曆。

paragraphs.en: Here's a personal example to show you how they work together:
paragraphs.zh: 這裡有一個親身經歷的例子,讓你看看它們是如何協同運作的:

paragraphs.en: I recently finishing writing my latest book (more details coming in a few weeks). Before I wrote the first word, I opened up a monthly calendar in Google Calendar. Then, I chose a target date by which I wanted to complete the first draft.
paragraphs.zh: 我最近剛寫完我的新書(幾週後會有更多細節)。在寫下第一個字之前,我先在 Google 日曆中打開一個月曆。然後,我選定了一個希望完成初稿的目標日期。

paragraphs.en: So far, so good.
paragraphs.zh: 到目前為止都還不錯。

paragraphs.en: Next, I created an action plan. I worked backward from the target date, and I determined how much I'd need to write each day to achieve my goal.
paragraphs.zh: 接著,我制定了一個行動計畫。我從目標日期往回推算,確定每天需要寫多少字才能達成目標。

paragraphs.en: Finally, I scheduled writing time on my daily calendar. I decided to write from 5:30 a.m. to 7:30 a.m.
paragraphs.zh: 最後,我把寫作時間排進了每日行事曆。我決定從早上 5:30 寫到 7:30。

paragraphs.en: Every day. Monday through Sunday.
paragraphs.zh: 每天都是,週一到週日。

paragraphs.en: Can you guess what happened?
paragraphs.zh: 你猜發生了什麼事?

paragraphs.en: I finished the first draft by the target date. But here's the best part...
paragraphs.zh: 我在目標日期前完成了初稿。但最棒的部分是……

paragraphs.en: It wasn't difficult at all. I didn't need to rely on willpower to write. Nor did I need to "get motivated" or inspired or whisper affirmations to myself.
paragraphs.zh: 這一點都不困難。我不需要依賴意志力去寫作,也不需要「找動力」、尋求靈感,或對自己喃喃唸著肯定語句。

paragraphs.en: I simply looked at the clock each morning, saw that it was 5:30 a.m., and started writing.
paragraphs.zh: 我只是每天早上看看時鐘,發現是 5:30,然後就開始寫作。

paragraphs.en: The rest took care of itself.
paragraphs.zh: 剩下的事情自然就水到渠成了。

paragraphs.en: That's how deadlines and schedules can work together to help you to achieve your goals.
paragraphs.zh: 這就是截止日期與行事曆如何協同運作,幫助你達成目標。

paragraphs.en: Try the following...
paragraphs.zh: 試試看以下做法……

paragraphs.en: Choose one of your goals. It doesn't matter whether it's to learn a new language, run a marathon, or write a novel. Any goal will do.
paragraphs.zh: 選擇你的其中一個目標。無論是學一門新語言、跑一場馬拉松,還是寫一本小說,任何目標都可以。

paragraphs.en: Open up Google Calendar and select a target date. Make sure it's practical given your available time.
paragraphs.zh: 打開 Google 日曆,選定一個目標日期。務必確保它在你可運用的時間內是切實可行的。

paragraphs.en: Next, create an action plan to hit that date.
paragraphs.zh: 接著,制定一個能達成該日期的行動計畫。

paragraphs.en: For example, let's say you want to learn a new language. Commit to listening for 30 minutes each day to podcasts that offer lessons in that language.
paragraphs.zh: 舉例來說,假設你想學一門新語言,就承諾每天花 30 分鐘聽提供該語言課程的 Podcast。

paragraphs.en: Finally, put that activity on your daily schedule. Try to schedule it at the same time each day.
paragraphs.zh: 最後,把這項活動排進你的每日行事曆。盡量每天在同一個時間安排它。

paragraphs.en: After a couple weeks, you'll find yourself doing it as part of your daily routine. Easy peasy.
paragraphs.zh: 幾週之後,你會發現這已經成為你日常routine的一部分了。輕輕鬆鬆。

paragraphs.en: That's it for now.
paragraphs.zh: 今天就談到這裡。

paragraphs.en: Stay well and talk soon,
paragraphs.zh: 保重,咱們再聊,

paragraphs.en: Damon
paragraphs.zh: Damon

paragraphs.en: P.S. If you're not sure how to set goals you'll actually achieve, check out my book The P.R.I.M.E.R. Goal Setting Method. It'll take you, step-by-step guide, through the entire process.
paragraphs.zh: P.S. 如果你不確定該如何設定真正能達成的目標,可以看看我的書《The P.R.I.M.E.R. Goal Setting Method》。它會用逐步引導的方式,帶你走過整個流程。

emails.subject: 3 ways to bounce back after breaking your habit streak

paragraphs.en: Hey 張振輝,
paragraphs.zh: 嗨 張振輝,

paragraphs.en: Forming new habits is tough.
paragraphs.zh: 養成新習慣是件苦差事。

paragraphs.en: Whenever we adopt a new habit, we must train ourselves to do something that runs counter to our current routines. These routines can be so deeply ingrained that they seem impossible to break.
paragraphs.zh: 每當我們想採納一個新習慣,就必須訓練自己做一些與目前routine背道而馳的事。而這些routine往往根深蒂固,幾乎讓人覺得難以打破。

paragraphs.en: I'll bet you can relate. See if the following scenarios sound familiar.
paragraphs.zh: 我敢說你一定有同感。看看下面這些情境是不是很熟悉。

paragraphs.en: * You commit to eating healthy. After doing so successfully for a week, you stumble upon your favorite junk food. You're unable to resist, and there goes your diet.
paragraphs.zh: * 你決心要健康飲食。成功執行一週後,你不小心遇到了你最愛的垃圾食物。你抵擋不住誘惑,於是你的飲食計畫就這樣泡湯了。

paragraphs.en: * You commit to writing in a journal each morning. After a month, you inadvertently skip a day. You don't mean to do so. You just forget, and there goes your month-long streak.
paragraphs.zh: * 你決心每天早上寫日記。一個月後,你不小心漏掉了一天。你並非故意,只是忘記了,於是維持了一個月的連續紀錄就這樣中斷了。

paragraphs.en: * You tell yourself that you're going to visit the gym each afternoon after you get home from work. And you do so for a few weeks. Then, one day, you arrive home feeling exhausted. It was a particularly stressful day at your job, and you want nothing more than to relax with a glass of wine and Netflix. There goes your gym routine.
paragraphs.zh: * 你告訴自己下班回家後每天下午都要去健身房。你確實做到了好幾週。然後有一天,你拖著疲憊的身軀回到家。那天工作特別累人,你只想來杯紅酒配Netflix放鬆一下。於是你的健身routine就這樣被打斷了。

paragraphs.en: All of us go through this when we adopt new habits. We stumble. We make mistakes. It's a natural part of the process.
paragraphs.zh: 每個人在採納新習慣時都會經歷這些。我們會跌跌撞撞,會犯錯。這是整個過程中很自然的一部分。

paragraphs.en: It doesn't matter how important the habits are. They might completely transform our lives. Yet we still manage to slip up.
paragraphs.zh: 無論這些習慣有多重要——即使它們可能徹底改變我們的人生——我們仍然難免會失手。

paragraphs.en: Frustrating, right?
paragraphs.zh: 很令人沮喪,對吧?

paragraphs.en: When this happens, don't beat yourself up about it. Don't think of these misfires as failures. Think of them as minor hiccups.
paragraphs.zh: 當這種情況發生時,別苛責自己。別把這些失誤當作失敗,把它們當成小小的顛簸就好。

paragraphs.en: Here are three things you can do to quickly get back on track. They've worked for me, and I'll bet they'll work for you, too.
paragraphs.zh: 以下是三件能幫你快速重回正軌的事。它們對我很有效,我敢說對你也一樣管用。

paragraphs.en: #1 - Take a small step back
paragraphs.zh: #1 - 稍微退後一步

paragraphs.en: One of the keys to adopting any new habit is to take micro steps. Start small and build slowly.
paragraphs.zh: 養成任何新習慣的關鍵之一,就是採取「微小步驟」。從小處著手,慢慢累積。

paragraphs.en: For example, suppose you want to jog for 45 minutes each morning. Start by jogging for 5 minutes for a few days. Then, jog for 10 minutes over the next few days. Then, do it for 15 minutes the following week. And so on.
paragraphs.zh: 舉例來說,假設你想每天早上慢跑45分鐘。可以先從連續幾天慢跑5分鐘開始。接下來幾天慢跑10分鐘。再下一週做到15分鐘,依此類推。

paragraphs.en: Now, let's say you miss a few days. No problem. Take a step back. For example, if you've been jogging for 30 minutes a day and slip up, commit to jogging for just 20 minutes tomorrow. Or even 10 minutes.
paragraphs.zh: 現在,假設你漏了幾天。沒關係,退後一步就好。舉例來說,如果你原本每天慢跑30分鐘卻失手了,那就承諾明天只慢跑20分鐘,甚至10分鐘也行。

paragraphs.en: Making a smaller commitment will help get you back in the saddle.
paragraphs.zh: 訂下較小的承諾,能幫助你重新回到軌道上。

paragraphs.en: #2 - Put the habit on your daily schedule
paragraphs.zh: #2 - 把這個習慣排進你的每日行程

paragraphs.en: Make it an appointment with yourself.
paragraphs.zh: 把它當作與自己的一個約定。

paragraphs.en: For example, let's say you're committed to practicing the guitar each day. But your life gets busy, and you abandon the habit.
paragraphs.zh: 舉例來說,假設你決心每天練習吉他,但生活變得忙碌,於是你放棄了這個習慣。

paragraphs.en: Get back on track by putting your daily practice session on your schedule. Don't just put it on your to-do list. Actually block off time on your daily calendar.
paragraphs.zh: 把每日練習時段排進你的行事曆中,藉此重回正軌。不要只是把它列在待辦清單上,而是要在每日行事曆上真正劃出時間。

paragraphs.en: Treat it like an important, can't-miss appointment.
paragraphs.zh: 把它當作一個重要、不可錯過的約會來對待。

paragraphs.en: #3 - Commit to doing just a tiny bit
paragraphs.zh: #3 - 承諾只做一點點就好

paragraphs.en: It's funny how the brain works. We pride ourselves on being rational, reasonable, and logical, but we can actually trick our brains into doing something it doesn't want to do.
paragraphs.zh: 大腦的運作方式很有趣。我們自豪於自己是理性、講道理、有邏輯的,但實際上我們可以「欺騙」自己的大腦去做它原本不想做的事。

paragraphs.en: This can be very useful when we're trying to form new habits and need to get back on track after screwing up.
paragraphs.zh: 當我們想養成新習慣,並在搞砸後需要重回正軌時,這一招特別有用。

paragraphs.en: Tell yourself that you'll do just a tiny bit.
paragraphs.zh: 告訴自己,你只需要做一點點就好。

paragraphs.en: For example, suppose you're committed to working out for 45 minutes a day. You have an entire workout regimen. But for whatever reason, you skip a day. You just don't feel like working out. Then, you skip another day. And another.
paragraphs.zh: 舉例來說,假設你決心每天運動45分鐘,你有一整套完整的健身計畫。但不知為何,你跳過了一天,就是提不起勁運動。接著你又跳過了一天,再一天。

paragraphs.en: After skipping workouts for an entire week, getting back on track may seem impossible.
paragraphs.zh: 整整跳過一週的運動後,重回正軌似乎變得遙不可及。

paragraphs.en: Try this: tell yourself that you'll just do five pushups. Forget your carefully-planned regimen. Just focus on doing five pushups.
paragraphs.zh: 試試這個方法:告訴自己只要做五下伏地挺身就好。忘掉你精心規劃的整套計畫,只專注在完成五下伏地挺身。

paragraphs.en: Once you start, your mind will want to continue. That's what I mean by "tricking your brain." It's like persuading your child to try a new food you're certain he'll love. Focus on getting him to take the first bite.
paragraphs.zh: 一旦你開始了,你的心智就會想繼續下去。這就是我所謂的「欺騙大腦」。這就像哄你的孩子嘗試一種你確信他會喜歡的新食物——重點是先讓他咬下第一口。

paragraphs.en: Adopting new habits is rarely easy. Often we have to change years of mental programming before we can accept the new routines. Missteps are inevitable.
paragraphs.zh: 養成新習慣很少是件容易的事。我們通常必須改變多年來的心智慣性,才能接受新的routine。失誤在所難免。

paragraphs.en: The good news is, you can easily bounce back if you slip up. Try the three "tricks" above. You may be surprised by how effective they are.
paragraphs.zh: 好消息是,一旦失手,你也能輕鬆地重回正軌。試試上面這三個「小訣竅」,你可能會驚訝於它們有多有效。

paragraphs.en: I've bent your ear long enough today. My next email will be much shorter. I promise. :)
paragraphs.zh: 今天已經佔用你不少時間了。我保證下一封信會短很多。:)

paragraphs.en: Talk soon,
paragraphs.zh: 咱們再聊,

paragraphs.en: Damon
paragraphs.zh: Damon

paragraphs.en: P.S. If you're struggling to form new habits, my book Small Habits Revolution can help. It describes, in step-by-step detail, how to adopt new habits and make them stick.
paragraphs.zh: P.S. 如果你正為養成新習慣所苦,我的書《Small Habits Revolution》能幫上忙。書中以逐步詳盡的方式,說明如何採納新習慣並讓它們持續下去。
